scenes.say: This is tallyagent. An A I staff member for a C A firm, working inside the Tally books the firm already trusts.
Sixty five percent of practices say staffing is their biggest problem. And every month, for every client, someone reconciles G S T R two B by hand, while input credit quietly goes at risk.
Everything you are about to see ran against a real TallyPrime. When we filmed it, Tally was down. The agent restarted it, cleared the licence screen, and carried on.
Every person has a role. A clerk drafts. A partner decides. And the software knows the difference.

A clerk asks for a sale in plain words. The agent checks the ledgers and the stock, works out integrated G S T from both G S T numbers, and before anyone approves, it notices six identical invoices already on that date, and says so.
The clerk cannot approve it. A partner signs in with a PIN, approves, and the voucher lands in Tally, with the partner's name on the audit trail.
This is the real TallyPrime. The agent opens the Day Book on its own, the partner approves, and the new sale appears on Tally's own screen.
There is no Baroda branch in these books. There is Vadodara, the same city by its other name. So it asks, instead of guessing.
One install serves the whole practice. Each client has its own books, its own queue, and its own consent. A client nobody has enabled cannot be written to at all.

A pile of scanned bills. Each one is read on this machine, and drafted, or set aside for a person. On bills photographed the way clients send them, every field read right, and the unreadable one was refused.
Then the headline. Every morning, the agent runs every client. It reconciles G S T R two B, drafts the missing bills, and puts everything that needs a person in one inbox, money at risk first.
A supplier who has not filed is not just flagged. The credit goes on a deferred ledger, and the follow up letter is already written.

This is how throughput grows. A partner lets a client's work earn hands off posting. After a run of clean approvals, that kind of entry posts by itself, never above what a person has approved. One correction, and it goes back to waiting.

Where X M L is not enough, the agent works Tally's own screens. The red ring goes to each field before it types, the caption names every key first, and a partner approves before Ctrl A accepts the voucher.
When Tally interrupts with a bill wise screen, the agent recognises it, allocates on account, and carries on. Anything it does not recognise, it stops on, instead of typing into it.
On the first of the month, one close pack. Negative cash, duplicate bills, and input credit at risk in rupees. And G S T R one, checked before it is filed.
Every sign in, every grant, every approval, is on a hash chained log. It verifies, so you know nobody altered it.
Writes are pinned to the books a partner enabled. The model can run inside your office. And nothing reaches a client's books without a name on it.
Your Tally. Two clients. Two weeks. tallyagent.
